proposal.hypothesis: The valid flattened-tile 32x64x64 scalar 4x4 candidate measured 0.033899 s mean, while the valid row-band and B-packed variants measured 0.035286 s and 0.072814 s. This experiment changes only the output row block to 64 while retaining the 4x4 register microkernel, 64-column/reduction blocks, first-reduction overwrite, and static tile ownership. A larger row tile may reuse each B panel across more output rows and reduce tile scheduling work; its larger footprint may instead hurt locality. The candidate is unmeasured.

retained: Replace the size-specialized reference traversal with a generic blocked GEMM using 64x64 output tiles and 64-element reduction blocks, with bounds-safe edge handling.
Use a scalar unrolled 4x4 output microkernel with sixteen local accumulators; initialize accumulators to zero on the first reduction block and load prior C values only on subsequent blocks.
Assign independent flattened output tiles to a static OpenMP loop, capping worker count by the caller's thread budget and tile count; retain serial behavior without OpenMP.
Do not pack operands or add explicit SIMD or ISA-specific code, isolating the row-block-size change.

proposal.hypothesis: The failed prior attempt passes n=32 but fails at n=128, consistent with reloading C on later reduction panels even though the partial register sums were never stored. This candidate retains each 4x4 microkernel's accumulators across all K panels and stores each output once. It also tests increasing the row tile from 64 to 128 while holding the 64-column and 64-K tiles, scalar microkernel, and flattened static tile ownership constant. Fewer tile tasks may reduce scheduling work at n=1024; reduced parallelism may instead hurt smaller sizes. Earlier valid flattened parallel and row-band means were 0.033899 s and 0.035286 s, respectively; no speedup is claimed before measurement.

retained: Keep the 4x4 scalar output microkernel and 64-element reduction panels, but retain register accumulators across every panel instead of rereading C before any partial output has been stored.
Increase the output row tile to 128 while retaining 64-column tiles and flattened static ownership of independent tiles.
Continue to cap OpenMP workers by the caller's thread count and available tile count, with serial fallback when OpenMP is unavailable or one worker is requested.
Retain bounds-safe scalar handling for incomplete tiles and write every C element on each call without a separate initialization pass.
